clue.text: It's put on a plate in holiday home around France and Germany

indicators.note: the holiday home goes around the letter for France, wrapping it

parts.note: a gîte is a furnished holiday cottage in France
F is the international vehicle code for France
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Something is presented on a plate at a French holiday cottage, with France and Germany nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts GITE round F, and D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Handed over on a plate means given freely without effort, which is what a present that has been bestowed is.

clue.text: Parcel and divide fruit up, impressing wife

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so the wife letter is pushed inside
in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to divide is to part
a fig is a fruit

explanation.surface: Split up some fruit and press it in, says the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcel' looks like a noun but is the verb, to wrap; 'up' turns both pieces together, as a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something is to wrap it up as a present, a verb sense matching the answer.

clue.text: Completely ties up loose 25 with decisive results

indicators.note: ties up means binds around, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: completely means fully

indicators.note: loose means set free and jumbled, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, the European Free Trade Association abbreviation

explanation.surface: Thoroughly tidying up loose ends leads to decisive outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'loose ends' hides that 25 is a cross-reference to EFTA, the answer at 25 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with decisive consequences is acting in a way that seals destiny, which the adverb expresses.

clue.text: So removing limits on consumer goods

indicators.note: stripping the outer letters off these words leaves a run inside them

explanation.surface: Thus restrictions on what shoppers can buy are lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, used in English to mean so or hence.

clue.text: Frequently ring us and another paper

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
us is the Financial Times, the paper setting this puzzle
The Times is another British newspaper

explanation.surface: The Financial Times often phones a rival newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper the puzzle appears in, the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning often, many times over.

clue.text: Invention suitable for entertaining US agents

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding inside

parts.note: suitable means fit
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: A fitting way to entertain visiting American agents is a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something invented by the imagination, a fabrication.

clue.text: Gobsmacked when fiddling friend's tax

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as FRIENDS, its S counted

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished to learn a friend has been cheating on their tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of friend's supplies an S to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobsmacked is British slang for astounded, and transfixed means rooted to the spot by shock or wonder.

clue.text: A weaver raised dough

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, which in a down clue reads the pieces bottom to top

parts.note: a loom is the machine that weaves

explanation.surface: A weaver lifts up bread dough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns A LOOM upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough is slang for money, as is this American word for cash.

clue.text: Make more plastic in small modern 4

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
4 across is an old word meaning frequently; its modern form is often

explanation.surface: A small modern four making things more malleable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modern 4' asks for today's version of 4 across's old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic here means pliable, so making more plastic is making something less rigid.

clue.text: It's worn by fitter after going out

indicators.note: after a night out the letters are in a disordered state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something a fitter wears after a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: A titfer is a hat, from rhyming slang 'tit for tat'; British rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase rhyming with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat is a thing worn on the head, and this slang name for one comes from Cockney rhyming slang.

clue.text: Playing a gig unfit could be this

definitions.text: Playing a gig unfit could be this

indicators.note: playing means performing with, rearranging these letters

explanation.surface: Performing a concert while out of condition would be tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a gig played unfit is exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a concert while unfit would be wearing, tiring work, which the clue as a whole describes.

clue.text: A pudding's sent back cold

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: a fool is a creamy fruit pudding; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A dessert is returned to the kitchen because it arrived chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit puree folded into cream, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in manner means distant and reserved, unfriendly.

clue.text: Not many recalled Tory leader's yarn

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this word reads backwards

parts.note: not many means few

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Few remember the Conservative chief's long story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns FEW into WEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Weft is the crosswise thread in weaving, a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Eat pudding, swapping parts for styptic lotion

indicators.note: swapping parts tells us to put the two pieces in the reverse of their clue order

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Eat dessert, but trade places, for a skin-tightening lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is British slang for pudding; the clue gives the two pieces the other way round, hence 'swapping parts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic stops bleeding from small cuts, which is what this post-shave astringent does.

clue.text: Groom drove celebrity up to collect female — they attract interest

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, signalling an anagram
to collect means gathering in, so one piece goes inside
in a down clue, up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A groom drove a famous person to pick up a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the definition or a noun but is the anagram signal; 'they attract interest' refers to bank borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks charge interest on borrowing beyond one's balance, so these debts accrue interest.

clue.text: A devoted fan takes laptop everywhere

indicators.note: takes means takes in, holding the extra letter inside

parts.note: a devoted fan is a lover of something
read as lap top: the top letter of lap is L

explanation.surface: An enthusiast carries a portable computer wherever they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laptop' is read as the top of 'lap', its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: All over means in every place, throughout.

clue.text: Filter out more than half of 13, for example

definitions.text: more than half of 13, for example

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strain out the first part of a lotion, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first six letters of 13 across spell AFTERS, a British word for pudding; a trifle is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifle is a layered British dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream, an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Life felt strange and ultimately unconventional

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, picking the last letter

explanation.surface: Life felt odd and in the end quite unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges LIFEFELT; 'ultimately' takes the D of 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of left field is an American baseball idiom for odd or unexpected, so the hyphenated form means unorthodox.

clue.text: Right half player lost a litre of blood antigen

indicators.note: lost means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written, before letters are removed
a gives A and L is the abbreviation for litre
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A right-half footballer has lost a litre of blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes A and L from HALF, leaving HF. A right half is an old football position.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhesus factor is a protein on red blood cells, an antigen that determines a positive or negative blood group.

clue.text: Island power overrun by Persian emperor

indicators.note: overrun by means covered by, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A great power is conquered by an ancient Persian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Mock self-contained man with dyke, thin on top

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for self-contained, used in property advertisements
King Offa of Mercia built Offa's Dyke, the earthwork along the England–Wales border

indicators.note: on top in a down clue means the first letter

explanation.surface: Ridicule a solitary man with an earthwork, his hair thinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' takes the T of 'thin'. Offa's Dyke is an eighth-century earthwork marking the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to jeer or deride them.

clue.text: Women left riots during the endless day of parades

indicators.note: during means within, so the pieces go inside
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

indicators.note: riots means wild disorder, so the letters of left are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women abandoned the riots during the endless day of marching.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twelfth, 12 July, is the Orange Order's marching day in Northern Ireland; 'riots' is the anagram signal, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twelfth is the annual July date of Orange parades in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Maritime growth economy

definitions.meaning: the sea pink, a plant that grows on coastal cliffs

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a seaside flowering plant and the virtue of spending carefully.

clue.text: Quietly moved backwards in mid-week

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Wednesday, abbreviated WED, is the day in the middle of the week
aft means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Something silently drifted back during Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: To be borne gently on air is to move quietly and lightly.

clue.text: When pub's closed a female trips over her mobile

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: tours are trips

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After closing time, a woman stumbles over her phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone but signals the rearrangement of 'her'; 'over' has the trips wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The period after official licensing hours when a bar is shut.

clue.text: This water is so turbulent at first — call in pontoon

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The sea is so rough here, at least to begin with, a shout goes up on the floating platform.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon looks like a floating jetty, but it is the British card game like blackjack, where a player says this to ask for another card.
explanation.definitionFit: In pontoon a player calls this word to receive another card from the dealer.

clue.text: The Chieftains tour only four countries now

indicators.note: the letters tour inside the word, held within it

explanation.surface: The Irish folk band plays just four countries these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chieftains were an Irish traditional music group. The European Free Trade Association now has four members: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviated trade association whose membership has shrunk to four nations.

clue.text: 3 disheartened you once

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letter, is removed

parts.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: Three people lost heart, as you did in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the number itself, not a cross-reference; 'disheartened' removes the middle R.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic pronoun for you, as in old prayers and poetry.

clue.text: He'll get time if he's busted

definitions.text: He'll get time if he's busted

indicators.note: busted means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is, so the word he is the fodder

explanation.surface: A man faces a prison sentence if he is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a robber who is caught gets time.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber who is caught will be sentenced to time in prison, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Hand over proceeds of theft in final match

indicators.note: over means covering, so the hand goes around the other piece

parts.note: a clenched hand is a fist

indicators.note: the proceeds of a theft are what it is turned into, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Hand over what you stole in the last game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over' reads as one phrase but splits: hand is FIST and 'over' wraps it round the rest. A Test is an international cricket match, usually in a five-match series.
explanation.definitionFit: In a five-match Test cricket series, the last game is the fifth.

clue.text: Computer files stayed instead, 15

indicators.note: the answer to 15 across means everywhere, read here as turned all over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: stayed gives SAT, and instead split as in stead puts it in STEAD

explanation.surface: Computer files remained in place instead, everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is splitting 'instead' as 'in stead'. The cross-reference to 15 across, 'all over', works as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of data held as files on a computer, a technical term.

clue.text: He may be accused of lacking fire protection

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the next word is removed

parts.note: a man who may be accused of a crime is an offender

explanation.surface: A man could be charged with having no fire safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes OF from OFFENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal fireguard in front of a hearth protects against embers.
